title: Torsion en cohomologie cristalline : notes manuscrites (s.d.), copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Théorème 8.5, conditional on crystalline universal coefficients, Poincaré duality and weak Lefschetz including torsion). X ⊂ P^r_k is smooth, projective and connected of dimension n over a perfect field k of characteristic p > 0. Y is a smooth section of X by a hypersurface of degree d. H^i(-) denotes crystalline cohomology over W = W(k). The subscript ss denotes the Frobenius-semisimple (stable, 'unit-root') part of a k-vector space with a p-linear endomorphism. This is an exact functor (Fitting decomposition). By Lemma 8.4.1 on the previous page, H^i_dR(X)_ss = H^i(X,O_X)_ss.

Step 1 (8.5.4). Let U = X − Y, which is affine. In H^{n-1}(X) → H^{n-1}(Y) → H^n_c(U), the module H^n_c(U) is torsion-free (Artin-vanishing analogue). So the vanishing cohomology E(Y) = Coker(H^{n-1}(X) → H^{n-1}(Y)) is torsion-free, hence free over W. Consequently 0 → H^{n-1}(X)⊗k → H^{n-1}(Y)⊗k → E(Y)⊗k → 0 is exact.

Step 2. Universal coefficients give rows 0 → H^{n-1}(Z)⊗k → H^{n-1}_dR(Z) → _pH^n(Z) → 0 for Z = X and Z = Y. Restriction maps the X-row to the Y-row. Take ss parts and apply the snake lemma. On ss parts, the middle vertical map is v: H^{n-1}(X,O_X)_ss → H^{n-1}(Y,O_Y)_ss. Its cokernel is the 'coherent vanishing cohomology' E(Y,O_Y)_ss. This yields
0 → Ker v → Ker t → (E(Y)⊗k)_ss → Coker v → Coker t → 0,
where t: (_pH^n(X))_ss → (_pH^n(Y))_ss.

Step 3. Via Gysin, H^n(Y) ≅ H^{n+2}(X) (Lefschetz), and t is cup with the class dξ of Y. This explains the first draft: by torsion Poincaré duality, t is dual to w: Tors^{n-1}⊗k → Tors^{n+1}⊗k (cup with dξ), with Ker t = (Coker w)^∨ and Coker t = (Ker w)^∨. Grothendieck's pencil correction replaces Coker w by (_pTors^n(X))_ss and ends the sequence at Coker v → 0. This is justified: (_pH^{n+2}(X))_ss is a quotient of H^{n+1}_dR(X)_ss = H^{n+1}(X,O_X)_ss, which is 0 since dim X = n. So the corrected sequence is
(8.5.1) 0 → Ker v → (_pH^n(X))_ss → (E(Y)⊗k)_ss → E(Y,O_Y)_ss → 0.

Step 4 (finite k). For a free F-crystal, dim (M⊗k)_ss is the multiplicity of slope 0, i.e. the number of p-adic unit eigenvalues of the linearized Frobenius. Grothendieck identifies this with the number of unit-root eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius on vanishing cohomology. He adds that this equals the ℓ-adic count, conditionally on algebraicity of Λ, i.e. a standard conjecture. The unit eigenvalues mod p are the eigenvalues of the p-linear Frobenius, equivalently, via the Artin–Schreier/Lang interpretation 8.4.2, of the inverse Frobenius generator of Gal(k̄/k) acting on an F_p-representation.

Step 5 (8.5.5). #unit-root eigenvalues on vanishing cohomology = dim E(Y,O_Y)_ss + (dim (_pH^n(X))_ss − dim Ker v), with the bracket ≥ 0. So the Hasse–Witt stable rank of coherent vanishing cohomology is a lower bound, and the defect is controlled by semisimple p-torsion in H^n_crys(X).

Purpose (next page). Show that for general hypersurface sections of degree d, the number of unit-root eigenvalues is constant on an open U_d of the parameter space. This generalizes the Hasse–Witt/zeta-function relation (Manin, Katz) from hypersurfaces in P^n to sections of arbitrary X, where crystalline p-torsion intervenes.
errors: The arrow out of Ker v is still labelled 'w', a leftover of the struck-out first version. In the corrected sequence it is the snake-lemma map Ker v → Ker t = (_pH^n(X))_ss, not w.

As written, the corrected (8.5.1) silently uses (_pH^{n+2}(X))_ss = 0, equivalently t_ss = 0 and Coker t = 0. This holds because H^{n+1}(X,O_X) = 0, but it is not stated. The first draft, with Coker w and Ker w, was the general form before this observation.
'W-module libre sans torsion' is redundant. The essential input, torsion-freeness of H^n_c(X−Y) crystalline, was conjectural at the time.

The crystalline vs ℓ-adic equality of unit-root counts is made conditional on the standard conjecture (algebraicity of Λ). It was later proved unconditionally (Katz–Messing 1974, using Deligne's Weil I).
Remark 8.5.7 (next page) leaves open whether Ker v = 0. It is in fact always true on ss parts (see 'missed'), so the bracket in (8.5.5) is just dim (_pH^n(X))_ss.

ideas.what: Frobenius-semisimple part of de Rham cohomology equals that of coherent cohomology (Lemma 8.4.1, used here).
Torsion-freeness of crystalline vanishing cohomology E(Y), via affineness of X−Y.
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline weak Lefschetz / Artin vanishing for compact supports
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (1974) for crystalline Lefschetz theorems; Artin (SGA 4) étale

ideas.what: Exact sequence relating the unit-root part of crystalline vanishing cohomology mod p, coherent vanishing cohomology, and semisimple p-torsion of H^n_crys(X).
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of p-rank of vanishing cohomology with Hasse–Witt stable rank, corrected by crystalline torsion
ideas.usually_credited_to: No exact attribution known; the torsion-free hypersurface case is Katz (SGA 7 XXII, Hasse–Witt and unit roots)

ideas.what: Number of unit eigenvalues of Frobenius equals the stable rank of the p-linear Frobenius mod p; equals the Gal-representation dimension.
ideas.modern_name: Slope-0 multiplicity / unit-root F-crystal; Katz's correspondence unit-root F-crystals ↔ p-adic Galois representations

ideas.what: Generic constancy of the number of unit-root eigenvalues for general hypersurface sections (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Generic p-rank / generic Newton polygon (Grothendieck specialization)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Barsotti 1970), Katz 1979; Illusie 1990 for generic ordinarity of complete intersections

missed.claim: Grothendieck's conjecture (Remarque 8.5.7, next page) that v is injective, so that Ker v = 0, has a short general proof on semisimple parts. A Frobenius-bijective element of Ker v lies in the image of H^{n-1}(X,O_X(−p^m Y)) for all m. By Serre duality and Serre vanishing this group vanishes for m large. Hence Ker v_ss = 0 and (8.5.5) becomes an exact formula: #unit roots on vanishing cohomology = dim E(Y,O_Y)_ss + dim (_pH^n_crys(X))_ss.
missed.quote: + (dim (_pTors^n(X))_ss − dim Ker v), où le terme entre parenthèses du deuxième membre est ≥ 0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a clean formula. It is equivalent to weak Lefschetz injectivity for H^{n-1}_et(−,F_p), which is presumably known to specialists, so the gain is modest.

missed.claim: An explicit formula expressing the defect between the unit-root count of vanishing cohomology and the Hasse–Witt stable rank of coherent vanishing cohomology by the semisimple p-torsion of H^n_crys(X). This generalizes Katz's hypersurface result to sections of arbitrary smooth projective X with crystalline torsion.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relevant to p-ranks and ordinarity of hypersurface sections (Illusie's generic ordinarity, Newton–Hodge questions). It can be rederived from étale Z_p cohomology, so its novelty is limited.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, carefully corrected exact sequence linking crystalline torsion to unit-root counts of vanishing cohomology, written before crystalline foundations existed. The tools are now standard (de Rham–Witt, étale Z_p comparison), and the result follows from known theory, so it is a notable unpublished detail rather than a surprise.
